Subject: Order form indemnity — proposed notice & triage approach

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this — BrightGear is reviewing the Order Form and one of our main sticking points is the indemnity / third-party claim notice process. We wanted to share a short preferred process so we can align on redlines quickly: 

- 48 hour initial notification from customer when they receive a third-party IP claim;
- Vendor must acknowledge within 2 business days and confirm lead counsel;
- Evidence checklist: sample prompts, logs, model version, config, and customer-provided artifacts (we can provide a checklist);
- Settlement: customer requires vendor approval before settling if it would admit liability or impose obligations on customer;
- Insurance offsets: customer expects vendor to use insurance first but cannot delay defense.

We can be flexible on caps and carveouts but need a fast triage and a single point of contact for evidence preservation so our security/compliance team can work with yours.

Attaching a short draft workflow (see attachment). Can your team route to legal + ops and propose the redline?

Best,
Marta Lopez
General Counsel | BrightGear

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear workflow. I copied Kimberly and Marcus from Legal and Sean from Ops so we can align internally and return a clean redline. High-level reactions:

- Acknowledgement SLA OK (2 business days) but we need to clarify what constitutes a valid "notice" (email+claim copy), otherwise there are ambiguity risks.
- Defense control: our standard position is to reserve selection of counsel to the vendor for consistency in defense strategy, but we can discuss a joint-teams approach for claims that touch customer data or configurations.
- Evidence checklist: happy to agree to a bounded list (requests tied to specific incident IDs and time ranges) — we cannot turn over full model weights or production-only secrets.
- Insurance offsets: we typically allow offsets but will not agree to insurance-first obligations that impede an immediate defense.
- Settlement consent: vendor consent will not be unreasonably withheld; propose a 10-business-day review window.

On Mon, Feb 20, 2028 at 09:03 AM Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Can Kimberly and Marcus propose specific redline language for the Order Form (and a short triage playbook we can share with your ops team)?

Draft plan below — please review and flag any business tradeoffs:

1) Notice: customer must deliver written notice with a copy of the claim and a short summary of the alleged infringing activity and a reference to affected resource(s). No start-the-clock on alleged oral notices.

2) Acknowledgement SLA: vendor to acknowledge in writing within 2 business days and identify primary contact.

3) Defense control / choice of counsel: vendor will assume defense and control of claims directly related to vendor models or services. If claim arises solely from customer prompts or customer-supplied content, vendor will cooperate but may seek reimbursement. For mixed claims, propose joint control with lead counsel appointment by vendor and inclusion of one customer counsel observer.

4) Settlement & consent: vendor will seek customer consent before settlements that impose obligations on customer; customer consent not to be unreasonably withheld. If vendor withholds consent, parties will engage escalation (GCs) within 5 business days.

5) Evidence & preservation: vendor agrees to preserve relevant logs, model version, request IDs for 90 days after notice; specific evidence requests limited to items reasonably necessary to investigate the claim (see attached checklist). No obligation to disclose proprietary training data or internal tooling.

6) Insurance & offsets: vendor may apply insurance proceeds; however insurance shall not delay defense activities. Proposed carving language for order form: "Insurance proceeds shall be applied to cover indemnified losses but shall not act as a condition precedent to vendor's defense obligations."

7) Caps & monetary allocation: for third-party IP claims, propose to keep standard Order Form liability cap but allow indemnity carveout for willful infringement found by final judgment (i.e., no open-ended uncapped exposure).

Sean — Ops: we need to provide the playbook (short, operational checklist) for evidence collection and a single shared SRE point who can pull logs on demand. Can you confirm availability and SLA?

-Kim
